name: MAGNOLIA OIL GAS CORP CLASS A

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The prior pass already did this work and landed on no_edge with a defensible +2%. Downgrading to no_model now that MORE is known — the deal is closed, the consideration is disclosed to the dollar, the termination risk is gone — is the analyst going backwards. Magnolia's own philosophy is public and unchanged, the acquired assets are proved developed rather than speculative, and roughly 2% nominal FCFF growth for the combined entity is as defensible today as it was on 2026-09-07. Refusing is not more rigorous, it is just less useful.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: WildFire's audited financial statements and the pro-forma balance sheet and income statement required by item 9.01, due by amendment within 71 days of 2026-09-14.
devils_advocate.already_visible: No, and that is the whole answer. The 2026-09-14 EX-99.1 is a four-paragraph completion notice with no financial detail; EX-99.3 and EX-99.4 are the related announcements; no 8-K/A has been filed; WildFire is private and has no public financials I can reach on any free source. The counter is right that knowing more should not produce a weaker output — but what I now know is specifically that the acquisition is irreversible and its financials are absent, which is a stronger reason to decline than the pending-deal uncertainty the prior pass was managing. I also checked the prior pass's second nominated observable, a beta regression with R-squared above 0.15: today's is 0.36 with R-squared 0.042, so that test still fails too.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Whether the combined entity is cheap or expensive. I do not know. The prior pass did not know either — it said so, in the words 'until pro-forma financials are filed, any FCFF base for the combined company is a guess and I have not manufactured one' — and then supplied a growth rate that the model turned into a fair value anyway. I am declining to repeat that step.

what_changed: The transaction the 2026-09-07 pass was waiting for has CLOSED, and I went and got the document that pass nominated. Its devil's advocate named the observable exactly — 'the WildFire closing 8-K and pro-forma financial statements' — and the 8-K filed 2026-09-14 for an event dated 2026-09-10 carries items 1.01, 2.01 (COMPLETED acquisition), 2.03 and 3.02. It states the purchase price: cash of $2,570 million subject to final customary adjustments, 32,203,000 shares of Class A common stock, and assumption of WildFire's 7.500% Senior Notes due 2029. Three things follow. First, the termination risk the prior pass listed as a key risk — HSR and title/defect thresholds to 2026-10-13, outside date 2027-03-12 — is resolved and gone. Second, cash consideration came in at $2,570M against the $2.65B the prior pass assumed. Third, and decisively, the pro-forma financial statements are STILL NOT FILED: no 8-K/A exists, and item 9.01(a)/(b) allows Magnolia up to 71 days. So the observable arrived, and what it says is that the one input needed to model the combined company is the one thing it does not contain.
consensus_case: Magnolia is a low-cost Eagle Ford/Austin Chalk operator with a conservative balance sheet, Brent near $107, a JPMorgan upgrade on 2026-09-08 and a Zacks #1 rank. On 2026-09-10 it closed the $4.06bn WildFire Energy acquisition, more than doubling its Giddings acreage with more than $100M of guided annual synergies, funded roughly half equity and half debt. The market is paying for a larger, still moderately levered operator with a longer oil-weighted inventory runway in the basin it knows best. Nothing in that case requires the engine's -6.3% implied FCFF decline to be wrong; the price is a claim about scale and inventory, not about decline.
base_case_rationale: No base case is offered, and this is where I now differ from the 2026-09-07 pass. That pass recorded no_edge with a +2% five-year FCFF growth assumption for the combined entity, reasoning from Magnolia's stated philosophy — low-single-digit production growth funded within cash flow — and flagged 'read the verdict, not the number'. I think that was the right call while the deal was pending and is the wrong call now that it has closed, for a reason the closing changes: the mismatch is no longer prospective, it is realised and measurable. 32,203,000 shares have been issued and $2,570M of cash has left the company, against a model whose enterprise value rests on a 2026-06-30 balance sheet showing $400.0M of debt and $295.9M of cash. Publishing a per-share fair value from a standalone FCFF history divided by a share count 32.2 million short is not a conservative estimate of the combined company; it is a number about no company at all. Where a structural input is broken and the schema cannot override it, the standing practice on this screen is to record no number rather than launder the error into a fair value.
key_risks: Enterprise value understated by roughly 40-45%: the engine's $6.2bn omits $2,570M of cash consideration, $500M of new 6.625% 2034 notes, $600M of assumed 7.500% 2029 notes and the resulting revolver draw

Market capitalisation understated by about $827M: the engine's ~237.5M shares reconciles to the 183,703 thousand on the 2026-06-30 10-Q plus the 53.3M July offering, but NOT the 32,203,000 shares issued as consideration on 2026-09-10
The +212% gap and 94th-percentile Energy rank that won this opportunistic slot come from a +19.7% revenue-CAGR baseline measured off the 2021 oil trough, applied to a standalone cash-flow history

Beta 0.36 with R-squared 0.042 gives a 6.8% WACC to a now-levered, more oil-weighted E&P — the prior pass set 0.15 as the R-squared bar before any gap on this name should be taken seriously, and it is still not met
Net debt goes from roughly zero to about $2.1bn on a company whose appeal was balance-sheet conservatism
watch_for: The 8-K/A carrying WildFire's audited financials and the pro-forma statements, due within 71 days of 2026-09-14 — the document that makes this name modellable and the single item on this list that matters
The Q3 2026 10-Q in early November: the first balance sheet showing combined debt, cash and share count, and the actual RBL draw
Whether the engine's share count picks up the 32.2M consideration shares from the Q3 cover page or continues to price ~237.5M
A beta regression with R-squared above 0.15 before any gap on this name is taken seriously
